title: Calixtus: hearing and weighing the Gospel is not above nature
source_text: XI. Quibus consona sunt ea quae alibi tradit idem autor. Id autem observandum est, inquit, posito quod Deus Evangelium revelaverit, & passim inter homines praedicari faciat per homines, non esse supra vires naturae quod quis Evangelium audiat, concipiat, consideret, & cum iis quae ab aliis, Judaeis puta vel Mahumetanis, tanquam divinitus revelata proferuntur comparet. In judicio de controversiis Theologicis quae inter Lutheranos & Reformatos agitantur, num. 33.
pass_a_gloss: XI. With which agree those things which the same author teaches elsewhere. But this is to be observed, he says, granted that God has revealed the Gospel, & causes it to be preached everywhere among men by men, that it is not above the strength of nature that one should hear the Gospel, conceive, consider it, & compare it with those things which by others, Jews say or Mahometans, are put forward as divinely revealed. In the judgment on the Theological controversies which are agitated between the Lutherans & the Reformed, num. 33.
pass_b_english: Thesis XI. What the same author teaches elsewhere agrees with this. 'Note,' he writes, 'that once God has revealed the Gospel and has it preached by people far and wide among people, it is not beyond the strength of nature for someone to hear the Gospel, grasp it, think it over, and set it beside what others, Jews for instance or Muslims, put forward as revealed by God.'
This is in his judgment on the theological controversies in dispute between the Lutherans and the Reformed, number 33.
